title: The spectrum of an algebraic extension is the limit over finite subextensions
statement: Let F⊆E be an algebraic field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. The spectra of the finite intermediate extensions, with maps opposite to their inclusions, form a cofiltered system. Its canonical cone with vertex Spec E is a limit in schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Every finite subset of an algebraic extension belongs to a finite intermediate field. Thus the inclusions of finite subextensions exhibit E as the filtered colimit of their rings; the source isColimitSubextCocone supplies precisely this universal property. Taking opposite categories gives a limit cone of opposite rings. The spectrum functor is a right adjoint and preserves limits. Apply isLimitOfPreserves Scheme.Spec to this cone, exactly as in the attached source definition. The proof is a single application of these general limit APIs.
